title: Slow requests, the RDD way
prompt: What does this program print? In the lesson's 12 requests, four took more than 100 ms: REQ-000004 (checkout-api), REQ-000005 (search-api), REQ-000008 (checkout-api) and REQ-000011 (search-api).
program:
slow = api_requests.rdd.filter(lambda r: r["latency_ms"] > 100)
names = slow.map(lambda r: r["service"])
print(slow.count(), api_requests.count())
print(names.collect())
hints: `rdd.filter` keeps the rows where the Python function returns `True`. Like a DataFrame transformation, it doesn't change what it started from.
`map` turns each row into whatever the function returns: here, one string per row.
`collect()` returns a Python list, in the same order as the rows. It doesn't remove repeats.
